translations.text: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I said, “I see a branch of a walnut tree.”
Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob, and every family of the house of [?].
Look at your ways in the burial ground, and understand what you have done.
And you said, “I am innocent. Let your anger turn away from me.” Look, I will bring you to judgment because you say, “I have not sinned.”

In those days, and during those days, they will call [?] “the throne of the Lord,” and all the nations will gather to her in the name of the Lord. They will no longer follow the desires of their evil hearts.
Your ways and your deeds have brought these things upon you. This is your wickedness: it is bitter, and it has reached into your heart.
And they are not wise. They are skilled at doing evil, but they do not know how to do good.
I looked, and there was no one, and all the birds of the sky had scattered.
Which of these things shall I forgive you for? Your children have abandoned me and swear by those who are not gods. I fed them, and they committed adultery and settled in prostitutes’ houses.
They became like stallions lusting after females, each one neighing for his neighbor’s wife.
This is what the Lord says: “Look, a people is coming from the north, and a great nation will rise from the ends of the earth.”
And you murder, commit adultery, swear falsely to support injustice, steal, and offer incense to Baal. You have followed foreign gods whom you do not know.
In his wealth.
But you, Lord, know me. You have seen me and tested my heart before you. Set them apart, then, for the day of their slaughter.
They have made it a ruined wasteland because of me. The whole land has been utterly ruined, because no one takes it to heart.
And I went to the Euphrates River, dug, and took the loincloth out of the place where I had buried it. And look, it had rotted and was no longer good for anything.
Tell the king and the powerful, “Humble yourselves and sit down, because the crown of your glory has been taken from your heads.”
Therefore, look, days are coming, says the Lord, when they will no longer say, “As the Lord lives, who brought the children of [?] out of the land of Egypt.”
I am the Lord who searches hearts and tests kidneys, to give each person according to his ways, and according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his deeds.
They made their necks stiffer than their ancestors’ necks, refusing to listen to me or accept instruction.
And it will happen, if you listen to me, says the Lord, that you will bring no loads through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, do no work, and keep the Sabbath day holy.
I will strike everyone who lives in this city, both people and animals, and they will die a terrible death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword and famine. But whoever goes out and flees to the Chaldeans who have besieged you will live. He will gain his life as a prize and live.

And to the house of David, this is what the Lord says: “Judge justly in the morning, act uprightly, and rescue the person who has been robbed from the hand of his oppressor, so that my anger does not flare up like fire and burn with no one to put it out.”
For if you truly carry out this command, kings who sit on David’s throne will enter through the gates of this house, riding in chariots and on horses, together with their servants and their people.
But if you do not carry out these words, I have sworn by myself, says the Lord, that this house will become a ruin.
If they had stood in my council and listened to my words, they would have turned my people away from their evil deeds.
Can anyone hide in a hiding place so that I cannot see him? Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the Lord.
This is what the Lord says: My words are like a blazing fire and like a hammer that breaks a rock.
The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Send word to Migdol, and deliver the announcement to Memphis. Say in Tahpanhes: Stand up and prepare yourself, for the sword has devoured those around you.
Because of the Lord’s anger, no one will live in her; instead, she will be entirely devastated. Everyone who passes through Babylon will be appalled and hiss at all her wounds.

The word that the Lord entrusted to Jeremiah the prophet to tell Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, when he was going to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the official in charge of the gifts.
Jeremiah wrote in a scroll all the disasters coming upon Babylon—all these words written concerning Babylon.
I have heard Moab’s insults, his contempt and his arrogance. His heart has become proud.
I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse for all the nations of the whole earth.

Did Hezekiah and all the people of Judah put him to death? Was it not because they feared the Lord and pleaded for the Lord’s favor that the Lord relented from the disasters he had said he would bring upon them? But we have brought great harm upon our own lives.

This was the place where King Zedekiah had imprisoned him, saying: Why do you prophesy, saying, ‘This is what the Lord says: Look, I will hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it’?
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
And I gave Baruch instructions in their presence, saying to him:

This is what the Lord says: In this place, which you say is a wasteland with neither people nor animals, in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem, which have become desolate, with neither people nor animals living there, people will once again hear:
This is what the Lord of hosts says: In this deserted place and in all its cities, people will once again hear of shepherds’ sheepfolds, where they settle their flocks.

You will die in peace. Just as they mourned your ancestors who reigned before you, so they will mourn you too and lament for you down to the realm of the dead. For I myself have spoken this word, says the Lord.
For this is what the Lord says: I made a covenant with your ancestors on the day I rescued them from the land of Egypt, from the house of their slavery, saying to them:
Today they turned back to do what is right in my sight, each one granting freedom to his neighbor. They made a covenant before me in the house that bears my name.

I brought them into the house of the Lord, into the chamber of Johanan son of Hananiah, the man of God. It was beside the chamber of the officials, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the courtyard.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
The descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab will never lack a man to stand before me throughout all the days of the earth.
Perhaps the house of Judah will hear about all these disasters that I plan to bring upon them, so that they turn away from their evil way, and I will forgive their injustices and their sins.
Perhaps mercy will come upon them in the Lord’s presence, and they will turn away from their evil way, for great are the anger and wrath that the Lord has declared against this people.
This is what the Lord said: “This is what you must say to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of me: Look, Pharaoh’s army, which came to help you, will return to the land of Egypt.”
King Zedekiah sent for him and summoned him secretly. He questioned him, saying, “Do you have a word from the Lord?” Jeremiah said, “Yes. You will be handed over to the king of Babylon.”
Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, who was in the king’s house, heard that they had thrown Jeremiah into the cistern. The king was in the courtyard of Benjamin.
All the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him. He told them everything the king had instructed him to say. So they remained silent, because they had not heard any word from him.

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, sent him away from Daman [?], when he took him in bronze chains among the exiles of Judah, from their governors [?], down to Babylon.
The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, “The Lord your God declared that he would bring these disasters upon this place.”

Johanan and all the army commanders with him took all the remaining people whom he had recovered from Ishmael: men strong in battle, women, the others, and the eunuchs. He brought them back from Gibeon.

“If you settle and remain in this land, I will build you up and establish you, and I will not tear you down. I will plant you and not uproot you, for I have relented over all the disasters I sent to bring upon you.”
He will kindle a fire in the temples of its gods, burn them, and carry them away. He will strip the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his garment, and he will leave in peace.
They did not listen to me or incline their ears to turn away from their wickedness and stop offering incense to other gods.

“Was it not the sacrifice that you offered in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem—you, your ancestors, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land—that the Lord remembered and that came into his mind?”
They captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and he pronounced judgment on him.
